caption: Fig. 1 Overview of GEM-GPT. a. GEM-GPT autoregressively generates molecular SMILES strings by conditioning on the transcriptional transition from a diseased cell state toward its healthy counterpart. A pretrained scRNA-seq foundation model, scGPT, encodes the diseased and healthy gene expression profiles, while the scGPT-derived cell-state embedding serves as the initial token embedding for cell type-specific molecular generation. b. Detailed architecture of a GEM-GPT block and the proposed deep fused attention mechanism. At each layer, the molecular hidden state is separately fused with the corresponding scGPT hidden representations of the healthy and diseased cell states. The difference between the resulting conditioned molecular representations is propagated to the next GEM-GPT layer, allowing the desired disease-to-healthy transcriptional shift to guide molecular generation throughout the network. The enlarged view illustrates the layer-level interaction between the trainable molecular attention module and the frozen scGPT attention module through concatenated key and value representations.

Fig. 2 GEM-GPT generates cell type-specific hit-like molecules from bulk compoundinduced gene expression profiles in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution cell-line settings. a. Schematic of the in-distribution (ID) cell-line benchmark using L1000 compound-induced gene expression profiles from 3 cell lines with a compound InChIKey-based split. b. Kernel density estimates of the similarities between generated molecules and their corresponding reference compounds in the ID setting. GEM-GPT shows distributions shifted toward higher similarities than the baseline models, indicating greater structural resemblance to the reference compounds. c. Schematic of the out-of-distribution (OOD) cell-line benchmark using L1000 compound-induced gene expression profiles from 20 cell lines with a cell-line-level split. d. UMAP visualization of control gene expression profiles from the 20 cell lines in the OOD setting. Dashed contours indicate the training and validation cell lines, illustrating the cell-line distribution shift between the training and test sets. e. Heatmaps of the average similarities between generated molecules and their corresponding reference compounds for each OOD test cell line and model. GEM-GPT achieves the highest average similarities overall, demonstrating robust generation from previously unseen cellular contexts. f. Mean Jaccard overlap between molecular sets generated within the same cell line and between different cell lines in the ID and OOD settings. ∆ denotes the within-cell-line minus between-cell-line overlap. The larger ∆ observed for GEM-GPT indicates a greater separation between within-cell-line and between-cell-line molecular overlaps, supporting stronger cell type-specific differentiation of the generated molecular sets in both seen and previously unseen cell lines.

Fig. 3 GEM-GPT generates potential gene inhibitors from bulk CRISPR knock-out transcriptomic signatures. a. Box plots of similarities between generated molecules and known inhibitors of 10 human gene targets. GEM-GPT generally generated molecules with greater structural similarity to the corresponding known inhibitors than the baseline methods. b. Violin plots of Boltz2-predicted binding probabilities for the subset of knocked-out genes whose corresponding protein targets are druggable enzymes with a single binding pocket. GEM-GPT generally generated molecules with higher predicted binding probabilities for the corresponding protein targets than the baseline methods. NS indicates that the difference between GEM-GPT and the corresponding baseline was not statistically significant, with P ≥ 0 . 05.

Fig. 4 GEM-GPT enables personalized and cell type-specific therapeutic design for OUD. a. Pipeline for generating candidate molecules from paired cell type-specific gene expression profiles of OUD patients and healthy individuals, followed by SEA-based search of OUD-related targets. b. Molecular cluster distributions of generated candidates across all OUD patients for astrocytes, microglia, ODC, and OPC. Differences in cluster distributions among patients within the same cell type indicate personalized molecular generation. c. Mean Jaccard overlap between molecular sets generated within the same cell type and across different cell types. ∆ denotes the within-celltype minus cross-cell-type overlap. GEM-GPT exhibited a substantially larger separation between the two conditions than GxVAEs, supporting stronger cell type-specific differentiation of the generated molecular sets. d. FDA-approved compounds absent from the training set identified among GEM-GPT-generated candidates associated with OUD-related targets through SEA-based target prediction, including naltrexone, naloxone, and clonidine.
